about.title: About
about.intro: ThisPlayShelf is a place to keep track of the games you collect, with the columns you care about, and to share your collection if you like.
about.who: ThisPlayShelf is built, run and maintained by one developer who simply wanted a nicer way to keep track of his own games. It's a hobby project he works on in his spare time, so there's no company behind it, just him and the occasional help from friends. You can see more of his work at {site}.
about.free: No ads, and your data is never sold. The free plan is meant to be enough for most collections, but an affordable Pro plan is coming for super users; the {pricing} page has the details.
about.data: You can export everything as spreadsheet files whenever you like, and delete your account at any time. The {privacy} page explains what's stored.
about.gamesTitle: Where the game info comes from
about.games: Game names, covers and details come from {igdb}. Games from the catalog keep their name, cover and details, so those can't be renamed. Games you add by hand are yours to name and edit.
about.contact: Found a bug, have an idea, or just want to say hi? Send an email to {email}.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: The short version: ThisPlayShelf keeps what it needs to run your account, sells nothing, and lets you take everything with you or delete it.
privacy.account: Your email address and password are handled by Amazon Cognito, Amazon's sign-in service. Your password never reaches ThisPlayShelf's servers: signing in proves you know it without sending it. If you continue with Google or Twitch, they tell Cognito your email address and whether it's verified. Nothing else from those accounts is kept, and an account with the same email is linked rather than duplicated.
privacy.stored: Your username and display name, your collections and everything you put in them, and when things were created. These live in a Postgres database run by Neon on Amazon's servers in the United States. Your email address isn't kept there.
privacy.visible: Private collections are visible only to you. Public collections, your username and your display name can be seen by anyone.
privacy.cookies: A cookie remembers your username so pages draw correctly while they load. Others remember your colour theme and whether the sidebar's collections are folded. Your sign-in is kept in your browser's storage. There are no tracking or advertising cookies.
privacy.speed: About a quarter of visits report how quickly pages load: anonymous timings, with no account or address attached. The server records which kinds of page were requested and how long they took, never what you typed.
privacy.others: Cover images load straight from IGDB, so IGDB sees your browser's address when you view them, as any website would.
privacy.controlTitle: Take it with you, or delete it
privacy.control: In {settings} you can export everything as spreadsheet files, or delete your account. Deleting removes your account and everything you've added. The database host keeps a few hours of history for recovery, after which it's gone for good.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.intro: ThisPlayShelf is free, and the free plan is meant to be enough for most collections. A small paid plan for people who want to go further is on its way, and the very biggest collections can get in touch.
pricing.maxBlurb: For the very biggest shelves, consider custom limits, set to fit your collection needs.
pricing.collections: {count} collections, plus Owned and the Wishlist
pricing.text: {count} characters per note or text field
pricing.importRows: CSV imports of up to {count} rows at a time
pricing.why: Although this is a hobby project, hosting anything isn't fully free and there are some costs involved. The database, sign-ins, domain and servers all cost a little something. The goal is to keep the free plan as generous as possible and provide as much value as we can without charging you anything. Hopefully it's all you'll ever need. But for any super user, the option is there to enhance your experience. Plus we may even add some time saving features in the future =).
pricing.whyPro: If you get real value out of the site and/or wish to support its development and continuation, the pro plan might be the best way to show your support.
pricing.limits: You'll see your usage as you go: on your collections page, in each collection and in Settings. At a limit, adding stops with a message saying which one. Nothing you've already added is ever deleted, whatever plan you're on.
